_meta.description: Prerequisite concept graph for Programming Fundamentals / Data Structures learning domain.
_meta.dependency_weight_note: All edge dependency_weights are domain-expert priors, not learned parameters. Values in [0,1] represent the estimated strength of prerequisite dependency. A weight of 0.9 means the target concept is highly dependent on the source. These are used as edge features in the GAT layer and are not presented as experimental findings.

nodes.name: Variables
nodes.description: Understanding of data types, variable declaration, assignment, and memory.

nodes.name: Conditions
nodes.description: Conditional branching: if/else, boolean logic, comparison operators.

nodes.name: Loops
nodes.description: Iteration constructs: for loops, while loops, loop termination, nested loops.

nodes.name: Functions
nodes.description: Function definition, parameters, return values, scope, and modularity.

nodes.name: Recursion
nodes.description: Recursive function calls, base cases, stack frames, and recursive decomposition.

nodes.name: Data Structures
nodes.description: Arrays, lists, stacks, queues, dictionaries, and their operations.

nodes.name: Algorithms
nodes.description: Sorting, searching, complexity analysis (Big-O), and algorithm design patterns.

edges.justification: Conditions require understanding of variables and their values.
Loops use loop variables and counters.
Loop termination conditions require understanding of boolean logic.
Functions often encapsulate iteration logic; loops appear inside functions.
Recursion is a special case of function calls; functions must be understood first.
Base-case reasoning in recursion relies on conditional logic.
Data structure operations are typically encapsulated in functions.
Traversal of data structures requires iteration.
Algorithms operate on data structures; sorting/searching requires data structure understanding.
